title: Building in public: why it forces durable competitive advantage, quality code, and great culture
summary: Jason Cohen argues that building in public isn't a risk to your moat but a forcing function. Public code gets judged so quality rises, and if copying is easy you must build non-technical, permanent advantages. Open pay and transparency push you toward a culture of autonomy, growth and purpose.

principles.text: Public scrutiny forces higher quality because ego, the desire to impress peers, is a universal motivator.
principles.quote: In this sense, **building in public would force you to create quality, artful code.**

principles.text: If your product can be copied, you must build a non-technical moat like a marketplace or network, whose value money can't replicate.
principles.quote: You are therefore forced to build some other, non-technical [competitive advantage](https://longform.asmartbear.com/moats/) into your business.

principles.text: Technical advantages are usually fleeting and copiers often do it faster and cheaper, so first to market rarely means winning.
principles.quote: But this is rare; typically a technical advantage is a fleeting advantage, because most technical things can be replicated.

principles.text: The most valuable company assets, like buyers and sellers on a marketplace, can't be replicated by copying software.
principles.quote: The value in these companies  [cannot be replicated with money](https://longform.asmartbear.com/startup-money/), which is exactly why those companies are valuable.

principles.text: Transparent pay removes the extra-cash lever, forcing you to attract talent through culture and mission, not mercenary compensation.
principles.quote: This forces you to build a company where great talent *wants* to work, where people are there for the culture and mission rather than as mercenaries.

principles.text: Great talent environments rest on autonomy, growth, and purpose.
principles.quote: in general they include **Autonomy** (i.e. freedom to explore, the control and empowerment to invent solutions to problems
